primitives.name: Dynamic Skill Gaussian Process
primitives.verbatim_quote: Method / model GP prior over each player's latent skill vector f_i with block-diagonal kernel K (independent players), combined with the Bradley–Terry logit likelihood P(y=1|f_i,f_j) = logit-1(f_i - f_j).
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'f_i': 'latent skill vector (dimensionless)', 'K_i': 'covariance matrix (dimensionless)', 'k(t_j, t_k)': 'time kernel function (dimensionless)'}
primitives.assumptions: Skills evolve smoothly over time; players' skills are independent; Bradley-Terry model holds for pairwise comparisons.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When temporal dependencies exceed kernel capacity or data sparsity causes ill-conditioned covariance matrices.

layer2.mapping: Maps player skill evolution through time using Matérn kernel, incorporating surface and environmental covariates into a structured kernel product.
layer2.telemetry: Match prediction log-loss and accuracy on held-out ATP data.

primitives.name: Laplace Approximation Inference
primitives.verbatim_quote: Posterior found via Laplace approximation: Newton's method on the mode, exploiting sparsity of the Hessian (only 4n nonzero entries in the 2n×2n likelihood Hessian), solved with sparse Cholesky (CHOLMOD via scikit-sparse).
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'Q(f|y,θ)': 'approximate posterior distribution (dimensionless)', 'H': 'Hessian matrix (dimensionless)', '\\hat{f}': 'mode estimate of latent skills (dimensionless)'}
primitives.assumptions: Posterior is approximately Gaussian; likelihood is sufficiently smooth; Hessian structure allows sparse solution.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When likelihood curvature deviates significantly from Gaussianity or numerical conditioning fails in sparse solver.

layer2.mapping: Isomorphic to variational inference in GSE's belief propagation engine for fast online updates.
layer2.telemetry: Convergence rate of Newton iterations and relative error in predictive variance.

primitives.verbatim_quote: Predictions via the standard GP predictive mean/variance formulas with an extra Hessian-correction term.
primitives.assumptions: Predictive distributions follow Gaussian form; Hessian correction improves variance estimation.
primitives.breakdown_regime: In high-dimensional or poorly conditioned settings where numerical stability degrades.

reasoning_traces.think:
The core innovation lies in replacing static Elo/Glicko models with a dynamic Gaussian process (GP) that encodes temporal evolution of player skills. The GP prior assumes smooth skill trajectories governed by a time kernel (e.g., Matérn), allowing for non-Markovian dynamics. Contextual variables such as surface type are embedded via a separate kernel component. The Bradley–Terry likelihood links latent skills to observed match outcomes. Inference proceeds via Laplace approximation, approximating the true posterior with a Gaussian centered at its mode. This yields computationally tractable predictive means and variances, crucial for real-time applications. The model’s strength stems from relaxing the Markovian assumption, enabling richer modeling of skill fluctuations over time and across environments. However, it requires careful handling of kernel hyperparameters and numerical stability during inversion of large covariance matrices.
